sections.name: File setup, repository, GET, POST
sections.title: Setup and storage object
sections.what: Loads response helpers, the document service, and the extraction tools. Sets the Node.js runtime and creates one storage object for extraction records when the file loads.
sections.why: Likely reason: one storage object is shared by all requests instead of being rebuilt each time.
sections.watch_out: The storage object is created when the file loads, so a storage problem may appear at first use rather than at startup.

summary: Web address to read saved text extraction results for one document, and to run a new extraction on it.
purpose: Lets the documents page show extracted fields and start an extraction on demand.
why: Reason not stated in the code. The AI step is kept behind its own address, which likely keeps it separate from simply viewing a document.
how: GET looks up the document and returns its saved extraction. POST checks the document exists, then runs the extraction service with the chosen provider and returns the result. Missing provider settings lead to a 503 response.
inputs: Case id and document id in the address. POST takes no body in the visible code.
outputs: JSON with a data field, or errors with codes DOCUMENT_NOT_FOUND (404) and AI_UNAVAILABLE (503, seen in the tests).
risks: Parts of the GET and POST lines are cut off in the source, so the exact steps could not be confirmed. Document text may be sent to an outside AI provider when one is configured.
debug: A 404 means the document service did not find the document. A 503 with AI_UNAVAILABLE means no provider is configured, so check the environment settings that choose a provider.
